precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:10
precepts.why:
Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 9:9
precepts.why:
“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” A help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living, something to his liking, something for him. God first brought every beast and fowl to Adam, and Adam named them all, because he was over them. Then it says, “but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Nothing yet was just for him.

So “the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”, took one of his ribs, “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High doing this for his son, and that is a gift. The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman made just for you, because it is not good for man to be alone.

Solomon says what to do with that gift: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Living joyfully takes application. It is something you have to make happen.

He goes on: “for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” God made this woman for you. She is the portion you have been given in this life and in all the work you do under the sun, so receive her as the gift she is and live joyfully with her.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 11:8-9
precepts.why:
Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Just as Adam had dominion over the creatures he named, he named her. So there is no confusion about why the woman was made, Paul says: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” “Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.”

People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? They do not know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. God created the woman for the man, and nobody can create or remake their own purpose in life.

So many people, men and women, spend their lives fighting against their God-given purpose. It is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not. And you wonder why you are dealing with spirits of depression and anxiety and always on edge: it is because you are fighting against your God-given role. You cannot change it, and trying only brings confusion.

Out of all the beasts of the field there was nothing fit for the man, so God made him a woman, and that woman has a purpose: help meet for her husband. Sometimes the help starts to think she is the purpose, that she is the house. No: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself; turmoil comes when you leave that place.

That is where it all went left. Eve knew the rule, but the serpent spoke to what was already within her: “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She wanted the position that was over her. Paul goes back to the beginning for the same reason: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” And Sirach says, “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” All she had to do was stay in her role and in order.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. But the first woman, the first created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife ain't? That is why the head has to keep reminding them of their place and role in the home.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:3
precepts.why:
Respect is taught in childhood, and it starts with “Honour thy father and thy mother.” Leviticus says it the same way: “Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am the Lord your God.”

The Lord understands the importance of structure, and it has always been there. You are to fear every man his mother and his father, and that goes on into old age. Don't think that once you turn 20 you don't have to listen. That power is always there: you honour your father and your mother.

And wives, once you become someone's wife, you also have your husband to deal with. The same power a father has over his daughter is handed over to her husband when he gives her away, so the respect a child learns for father and mother is the first line of the respect a wife owes her husband. That is how honouring father and mother connects to a wife respecting her husband.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 5:16
precepts.why:
Moses repeats the commandment: “Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

It was so important for them to honour their father and mother so that their days would be prolonged, so they would not die, and so it would go well with them in the land. The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation.

When there is dysfunction, anything not aligned with how God set it up, there are going to be problems, and it affects the whole nation. Certain households affect other households. If your house is out of order and you are best friends with so-and-so, your kids play together and learn the same bad behaviours. If a sister is a gossiper running from home to home and she is your wife's best friend, it is only a matter of time before your wife is called a gossiper too. Same with you: kick it with the murmurers and you will murmur.

You will infect the nation if your household is not in order. God is about order, always has been. A child raised in a household where the father and mother both understood the laws of God, operated within their roles and demanded obedience to God is more likely to carry that legacy on. Everybody still makes a choice, but the probability follows the household.

precepts.label: Luke 2:21-24
precepts.why:
In Acts 15 certain men came down from Judea and taught, “Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” Why does it say after the manner of Moses and not just circumcision? Leviticus 12 shows the manner of Moses. A woman who “conceived seed, and born a man child” is unclean seven days; “in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised”; she continues in the blood of her purifying thirty-three more days, forty in all for a boy and eighty for a girl. When the days are fulfilled she brings a lamb and a pigeon or turtledove for a burnt offering and a sin offering, and if she cannot afford a lamb, “two turtles, or two young pigeons”. The priest makes the atonement, and the offering covers the child as well as the mother.

Luke 2 confirms it with Mary and Christ. Mary conceived seed and bore a man child. “And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” That is the eighth day of Leviticus 12.

“And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord”, because “Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”. Then comes the offering: “to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.” Those are the offerings Leviticus 12:8 names.

So behind circumcision after the manner of Moses comes sacrifice. It is circumcision with the eighth day, the days of purifying and the offering for the woman and the child all tied together. That is what the men from Judea were pressing on the Gentiles, and that is why the scripture calls it the manner of Moses.

precepts.label: John 7:22
precepts.why:
If circumcision after the manner of Moses is circumcision with sacrifice, is all circumcision of Moses? Christ answers it: “Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man.”

Moses gave it to them, but circumcision is not of Moses. It is of the fathers, of Abraham, who was the one first circumcised. So when Acts 15 says circumcised after the manner of Moses, that is not the same thing as the circumcision of Abraham.

There are two different things here: circumcision of the fathers, and circumcision after the manner of Moses with the sacrifice of Leviticus 12 behind it. Seeing that difference is what opens up what the Pharisees were demanding and what Paul was fighting in his letters.

precepts.label: Genesis 17:24-25
precepts.why:
“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” “And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.”

Abraham was not circumcised on the eighth day after he was born; he was ninety-nine. Ishmael was thirteen. There was no eighth day, no days of purifying and no sacrifice. That is circumcision of the fathers, not circumcision after the manner of Moses.

The Pharisees wanted circumcision and sacrifice together, after the manner of Moses, because sacrificing was their bread and butter. As more people followed Christ, more of them stopped sacrificing, and if the people stop sacrificing, the Pharisees cannot eat. So they went into the churches saying you have to be circumcised to be saved. That is not what the Bible, Christ or the apostles taught. They were trying to put back on the people the yoke that could not be borne, the same one Peter asked about: “why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?”

precepts.label: Genesis 21:1-5
precepts.why:
“And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said”, and “Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.” Sarah conceived in old age and Abraham named the child Isaac. Then: “And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.” “And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.”

Isaac was circumcised on the eighth day, as God commanded, but this was long before Moses. There is no reading of them going and sacrificing animals for it. So even eighth-day circumcision here is not after the manner of Moses. There is circumcision of the fathers, and there is circumcision after the manner of Moses, which carries the sacrifice.

That is how Paul can say in Galatians 5, “if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.” He means circumcised after the manner of Moses, back under the yoke of bondage, taught by the Pharisees that you must be circumcised and sacrifice an animal to be saved. “For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.” Once the temple was destroyed and the priests scattered, that man had no way to keep it and was finished.

“Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.” Christ's sacrifice does away with the animal sacrifice, so whoever runs back to animals to atone for sin rejects what Christ did on the cross. Paul is not throwing out the commandments. He is rejecting the sacrifice that was bewitching the Galatians. So “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.”

precepts.label: Hosea 4:1-2
precepts.why:
Leviticus warns that if a daughter is prostituted, “the land become full of wickedness.” Hosea shows what full of wickedness looks like: “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” Controversy means against: the Lord is against how we live. It speaks mainly of the northern kingdom, but all of us are doing this now.

No truth: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Truth is the Bible, the laws. Nobody in the land is adhering to “Do not prostitute thy daughter”; nobody is paying attention to it or bringing that precaution into the land. No mercy: people get killed over this. Brothers have gone to jail and been shot down over it. No knowledge of God, meaning his commandments: the priest's lips should keep knowledge and the people should seek the law at his mouth, and they are not getting it at all.

“By swearing, and lying”. We heard complete lies two weeks ago: a man told everybody that nobody had told him to leave the sister alone, to make it look as if the leadership didn't know what was going on. Brothers had to stand up, bring him right back to his lying statement, and correct his wicked ass in front of everybody, so nobody would think he had a toe to stand on to justify the evil he did. Then: “and killing, and stealing”: we saw that in the videos.

All of it because the woman was taught to let her behind hang out. The Bible gives a dress code: cover your ass. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows that when the clothes come off, all kinds of things go on. David saw Bathsheba, and he lost it all. Then: “and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”. People get stabbed and shot up, all because she had her clothes off in the street. Do you see the connection?

So “full of wickedness” means literally full of wickedness: that is what you get when God's laws are not taught, no Bible, no scruples, no laws. Having kids through backdoor marriages produces madness like this. That is done here. You're going to do it right or you ain't going to do it at all; nobody is holding a ceremony over fornication. It starts with the fathers and mothers, who must not prostitute the daughter, because the enemy goes after the women: mess them up and the children are done.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:36-37
precepts.why:
This is where the breaking of “the pride of your power” leads. “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies”. Into their minds: mentally and spiritually, you are going to be broken down. Then “the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: no courage. And “they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

“And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” Think about that spiritually. Take 2026. When black people get mad at other black people, do we show each other mercy, or do we go full-fledged? We even came up with terms for it: turning up, going savage, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward white police, or the other nations, or the Chinese? Not at all. We will stand and be aggressive with each other all day long, cuss each other out, beat each other up, kill each other. But we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody. The point is that the spirit is not the same toward the nations as it is toward each other.

That faintness is on the face of the African brother who said the colonizers left too early, that we are not prepared to rule ourselves. Not only defeated but subdued: low self-esteem, lack of confidence, self-hate, no faith in his own people. It is seen in a whole country left to itself that looks to the white man, to foreign aid and loans, to save it: a mall built under Chinese direction with not a brick out of place, while what our people build for ourselves has uneven steps and lopsided houses. You can’t do nothing right for yourself. That is what comes of low self-esteem.

So this is the fruit of verse 17, “they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you”, and of verse 19, the pride of our power broken. These are the minds the Lord is going to use our brothers to change.

precepts.label: John 10:30
precepts.why:
“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” One mind, one body: we start with the order first. The Lord our God is one Lord, and Christ shows what that oneness looks like: “I and my Father are one.”

Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No. They are on one accord. Two persons, the Father and the Son, and yet one, because the Son is in full agreement with the Father.

That is what we as a body have to be: one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this body, in this congregation: because we are one. Many of our people today have a social religion, more like a superstition, believing what society told them to do. We rely on the scriptures and believe on the Lord as it is written, and the scripture says the Lord is one and Christ is one with him.

precepts.label: John 5:30
precepts.why:
How are Christ and the Father one? Christ does what his Father tells him to do. “I can of mine own self do nothing”: Christ said it himself. “as I hear, I judge”: as I'm told, that's what I do. “and my judgment is just”: the things he does are justified, “because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He didn't do what he wanted to do; he did what the Father told him to do. You see how that works? He says, I don't do what I want to, I do what the Father tells me to, and yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.

That is the oneness of Deuteronomy 6:4. Being one is not everybody doing their own will; it is every member doing the will of the one who is over him. That is how Christ is one with the Father, and how the body is one with Christ.

precepts.label: John 14:20-21
precepts.why:
Christ warned of his departure, when he would no longer be with them in the body: “At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.” What does it mean? Christ does what his Father tells him to do, Christ comes and tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments.

“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.” What commandments? The Father's commandments, all of them. We ain't Christians up in here picking and choosing and cherry picking, hopping and skipping around. Everything the Father told us to do: those are the commandments. The one who has them and keeps them is the man or woman that loves Christ, that loves the Lord.

“and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.” He is explaining the manifestation, how you receive the Holy Spirit. In order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High God and his Son.

That is how we keep the first commandment, to “love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”: by keeping his commandments, and being one with the Father and the Son as they are one.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 7:23-25
precepts.why:
When a man takes a wife and says, “I took this woman, and when I came to her, I found her not a maid”, who is the accusation against? The father. It is his household. He brought his daughter forth saying, this is my daughter, she is a virgin, I have taken care of her, I have watched over her.

That is why Sirach speaks to fathers: “Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth. Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.” You are not supposed to be your children's friend. You are their parent, over them, the head of the household, losing sleep watching over your children. A daughter learns order from the household in the beginning, and her father is the first form of respect she has: honouring her father and her mother. Show yourself cheerful and you begin to blur the lines, and once the lines are blurred, so is her perception of authority. So when she gets older, how is she going to deal with her husband?

“Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter”. It is weighty because the man now has the power you had over your beloved daughter: the little girl you brought into this world, watched after and lost sleep over. Her clothes, her food, her home, where she lays her head: he is in charge now. If I marry my daughter to a crazy negro, I failed; I did not vet him. So if I am going to give that power to somebody, I am damn sure going to make sure he is going to do right by her. That is the father's job, to make sure he is the one.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:32
precepts.why:
“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed, a chance we might get lynched. And not only the lives of the mothers and fathers were in doubt; our sons were in doubt too. That is why verse 32 is read here: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.”

That could have happened at any moment, any day. Your son ripped out of your arms to be sold to Master so-and-so, and you would never see your children again. From the day that child was born until the day someone said, I want that one as a slave, the parents lived with it, and they had nothing to say about it. “and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: they watched their sons get taken away and watched their daughters get taken away. That is the failing of eyes and the sorrow of mind of verse 65: no way to change your reality, no future you can see for your children.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand”: no might in our hands to stop it. And there was no alcohol for them. A bottle of whiskey would not have stopped that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord was still going to be with us somehow, some way. So they could not off themselves, because a generation was going to come from them, from the wife and from the husband, and our seed would continue while they went through trauma after trauma.

It took faith to make it from morning to night and night to morning, and they did not even have the truth the way we know it today. They pushed through all that evil and ugliness so that you and I could sit here today. So what excuse do we have? We cannot leave our post to drink and get high, or put our head inside a bottle and a crack pipe, when our forefathers endured this and kept pushing.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:3
precepts.why:
What is going on in 1 Samuel 15? The Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy all the Amalekites and everything they have, every last one of them. The Lord told Saul, wipe these devils out. And he didn’t do it.

The commandment was total: “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” All that they have. All means everything.

Now hold that against Saul’s answer in verse 20: “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.” Wait a minute: the king is still alive. What do you mean you followed the commandment of the Lord? Saul is playing the defensive, justifying himself, making excuses.

Then verse 21: “But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal.” It wasn’t me, it was the people, it was their fault; I couldn’t do nothing about it. That is bashfulness: you don’t take accountability. The commandment said spare the sheep and oxen not, and Saul brought them back and blamed the people.

So Samuel answered, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” To do what you were told is better than coming back saying, my bad, I thought I understood what you wanted, I decided to do it this way. You fulfill the commandment you were given, and if there is a problem, you say something.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:28
precepts.why:
Saul finally confessed in verse 24: “I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, or you don’t want them to be mad at you, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you to the left and to the right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.

Then verse 28: “And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” Damn.

That is what the bashful spirit costs. Verse 23 already said it: “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” When you are in that spirit the Lord can’t use you; you are not a good leader. Leadership may see something in you and put you in a position, and then when we question you on certain things you make excuses, or you separate yourself into a bubble with the men under you. You are bashful, you are bringing up a bunch of bashful brothers under you, and you are keeping the brothers under you hostage.

The Lord had made Saul king “When thou wast little in thine own sight”, when he thought he was a nobody. And because he feared the people and would not obey, the kingdom was torn from him and given to his neighbour, David, who was better than he.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:2
precepts.why:
“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what is that going to do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: so are they that are under him. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever man the ruler is, like King Saul, such are all that dwell under him.

Take an example. Some brothers have been here six months, a year maybe, not long, still in regular clothes. Some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. Those young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. So if you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, what does that communicate to them spiritually? That they can be timid, shy, fearful and bashful too. You don’t have to say nothing; your spirit is telling them, it’s okay to be like this, the officer can be fearful and timid, so I’ll follow his example, now I know how to move around in here.

It shall not be so. It shall not be so in here.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 17:12
precepts.why:
Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 1:7-8
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Bible says the Lord never gave us that spirit. So the fear Saul had when his heart greatly trembled goes back into a lack of faith.

“But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” We are supposed to have the spirit of power, love and a sound mind.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ. The bashful brother is ashamed and afraid; the one who has God’s spirit partakes of the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:28
precepts.why:
“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.” This is the level we have to get to: where we are not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, the one who can kill body and soul in hell.

Saul feared the Philistines and feared the people, and not the Lord. So, back to 1 Samuel 28:6: “when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. He went to the witch at Endor, the same kind he had put out of the land, and Samuel told him, “the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” Because he was bashful, self-willed, easily manipulated and made excuses, he lost the kingdom. Fear the Most High, not man.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 18:10-11
precepts.why:
This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke: “There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” The Lord said none of these would be found among Israel.

Saul had just rid the land of all of them: the soothsayers, the witches, the familiar spirits and the wizards. That is what the woman at En-dor throws back at him: “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You trying to get me killed.

Now the Lord has stopped answering him, “neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets”, and the same man who cut them off says, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Find me a wizard so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place. He is double-minded, breaking the very commandment he had enforced, and he disguises himself and goes by night so no one will see it.

That is where bashfulness leads: self-willed, disobedient, deceitful, making excuses, easily manipulated. Samuel tells him the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” The Lord rent the kingdom out of his hand and gave it to David, and Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day. “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness.” Saul never believed in himself, so he never believed God; he had Samuel's counsel the whole time and would not listen, and when that guidance was gone he ran to the very thing the law forbade.

Solomon’s mind was on the people. precepts.why:
“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:22
precepts.why:
The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him are going to be.

So when you see these other camps that look disorganized, that are talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders, and that is what you will see. When you see us traveling all over the world, building institutions, organizations within the organization, look at our leaders. We are the representation of our leadership.

When we go to Chicago we are not on film eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight. How is that a leader of a congregation? You will never see a bishop or a deacon put out a video like that. When we went to Chicago, we went to O’Block teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. You are who your leader is. That is why everybody wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but what they do not understand is that Christ is at the head and we are all following Christ. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:48
precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:2
precepts.why:
This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

precepts.label: Isaiah 27:12-13
precepts.why:
“Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.” That is the one verse they might run with: see, Egypt is his people and Assyria is his people, so the Egyptians and the Assyrians are saved too. No problem. Go over a few chapters and see where this Egypt and Assyria are.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.” Gathered one by one: who? The children of Israel.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown”: that is Christ coming. “And they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt.” Earlier it said Egypt and Assyria; here it is the land of Assyria and the land of Egypt, and the ones coming out of them are the children of Israel. So who is “Egypt my people” and Assyria? Israelites.

“And shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem.” My people in Egypt and my people in Assyria means Israel in those lands, scattered there and gathered out one by one to worship at Jerusalem. That is how precepts work: you don't build a doctrine for another nation on one verse.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:11
precepts.why:
Just in case Isaiah 27 is not enough, beat a dead horse. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” That is the same gathering we read in Isaiah 27.

From where? “Which shall be left, from Assyria”: my people. “And from Egypt”: Egypt, my people. “And from Pathros”: still Egypt, my people. “And from Cush, and from Elam”: Elam is Iran and Pakistan, my people. “And from Shinar”: Shinar is Iraq, my people. “And from Hamath”: Syria, my people. “And from the islands of the sea”: the islands, whether the Mediterranean or the Caribbean. That is his people.

It names Assyria and Egypt right there with the rest, and in every one of those places it is the remnant of his people that he recovers, not the nations of those lands. So when Isaiah 19 says “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands”, it is speaking of Israel scattered in Egypt and Assyria, whom the Lord recovers the second time.

precepts.label: Zechariah 10:6-10
precepts.why:
One more, just in case. “And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them.” Bring them again: that is the second time, the recovering of Isaiah 11. “For I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: as though they had never been in captivity. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad.” “I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them.” Both Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim: he will gather all twelve tribes. “And they shall increase as they have increased. And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria.” Bring who again? All twelve tribes, out of Egypt and out of Assyria, the same as Isaiah 11:11. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them.”

So what does “Egypt my people” and “Assyria the work of my hands” mean? It means Israel in those lands. That makes four scriptures, and there is no arguing with it. That is called precepts.

precepts.label: Job 8:8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 51:20 says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. What other people on the planet are at the head of every corner on the streets? That's us: in Miami, in the Bronx, in all the hoods and all the ghettos throughout the whole earth. We fainted, we are hid in prison houses, and we are on every corner. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

Christ showed what comes out of it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

Yet Solomon says, “All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes”. Every one of us thinks we are righteous. Ask them: me? I ain't do nothing. Covetous spirit? Hatred? Oh, no. Judas would have said the same. All our ways are clean in our own eyes.

“but the Lord weigheth the spirits.” The Lord sees everything, and you cannot hide from the Most High. You can fool the deacon, you can fool the bishop and the leadership, but the Most High sees you, and you are not fooling yourself either. You know where you were last night, why you never called the brother back, and why you told her to hush before you answered the phone.

That is Jeremiah 17:10: “I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins”. Only God can search the mind, and he weighs what is really in it, not what we show each other. Read on: “Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.”

Six days a week, Sunday to Friday, we do not know where you are or what you are doing. So what are you doing when you are not here? You cannot fool the Most High.

Paul says the same: “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit”. The one who searches the heart is searching the mind. And that verse tells you there are two: the spiritual and the physical man. There is a war, the spirit against the flesh, wicked against righteous, darkness against light.

That war will never be over until Christ comes back or you die in this. Some want it to be over and ask why there is so much evil in their head. Maybe because you are not reading enough. Brothers who do not know the scriptures will be the ones to betray you, because when they come to him he will fall. Ask yourself when the brother you talk to during the week last talked scripture with you. The Lord searching the heart gives every man according to his ways: not the deacon's way or the bishop's way, but yours. You are your own biggest enemy.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:4
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says “Flee out of the midst of Babylon”, and Revelation says the same thing: “And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people”. Revelation, Zephaniah and 2 Corinthians are three scriptures saying the same thing.

Come out of her, my people. Get your head out of Christianity. Get your head out of the philosophies. Get your head out of this thinking that your vote is going to mean something. You Israelites, you better get your mind right in terms of what the Most High is about to bring on this earth.

“that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” That is the “be not cut off in her iniquity” of Jeremiah: don't be partakers of her sins, and don't be destroyed when that evil comes. Zephaniah is saying the same thing with “Before the decree bring forth”: so that you don't get caught up in the judgments. That's the point.

And the way out is the order the Lord gave: gather together, O nation not desired. He is not asking; that is a commandment, a direct order. None of the nations desire us, none of them. So we are obligated to come together in righteousness and to follow the programme in this Bible. We are in the time of the Lord's vengeance now, and coming out of her is how every man delivers his soul.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-2
precepts.why:
Zephaniah gives the order: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. This is why Jeremiah says, flee out of the midst of Babylon: flee out of the midst of the philosophies of Babylon the Great. It is not necessarily talking about getting on a plane and going somewhere, because this whole earth is corrupted. It means come out of the philosophies of how this system has got us thinking. That is the whole point: how we think.

“Before the decree bring forth”. In other words, that ye receive not of her plagues, as Revelation says. It is saying the same thing in different words. Before the decree bring forth means before the destruction comes. “before the day pass as the chaff”: before the destruction. “before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. You have to do this so that you do not get caught in those things.

That is the “be not cut off in her iniquity” of Jeremiah 51:6: be not cut off, be not destroyed when the chaff goes through. “for this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance”, and we are in that time now. He is slapping the heads of these leaders, making them look stupid and crazy, in our presence.

And how do we return? Obey his commandments and organise, as the scriptures say. Become that mature nation in exponential growth; learn how to be an organised nation among ourselves, so that when we get the kingdom we will know how to act and how to operate as a nation. We are in the training ground. We were brought into captivity to learn a lesson, because we did not want to serve our Lord; when we learn it well, we come off our punishment and enjoy the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 6:17-18
precepts.why:
Paul is saying the same thing as Jeremiah and Revelation: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”. Separate your thinking from their thinking. You are not supposed to be hanging around them, hanging out with them. That is wrong. I don't give a damn what they tell you. That is wrong. The Lord did not bring us over here for us to be hanging with them and all of that.

I know that sounds like some serious racist talk, but you are the victims of every level of racism. So what the hell is wrong with you? We are the victims of every racist attack, yet when we say stay away from them, all of a sudden we are racist. The hell with you and your mama. My sons end up dead messing around with you, and I am supposed to worry about your damn feelings? The hell with that.

“and touch not the unclean thing”. If you continue to mess around in these philosophies, with their religions, with their politics, with any of that stuff, it shall pollute you and you will be destroyed by it. “and I will receive you”: we will be received in the Most High's nation.

“And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” He is building that kingdom when you come away from them. That is the organisation right there. Like the scriptures say, some will lose mothers, some will lose sons, daughters, fathers. You will lose these things, but when you come into this truth you will gain them sevenfold, tenfold. Ye shall be my sons and daughters because I am gathering you up, like Zephaniah said, and what you lost you are going to gain it all back again. That is how every man delivers his soul out of the midst of Babylon.

That great red dragon is Edom, Idumea, cast out of his rulership. Whether we are ready or not, the Most High is going to bring this to pass, so we do not need to be playing games.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 18:14
precepts.why:
The proverb was, “The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”: the present generation punished for the offences of their forefathers. The people were prone to plead their innocence: listen, I am this way because my father was this way. But the Lord said, “ye shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.” I am not letting you use the fact that you have been through intergenerational trauma, or that your fathers weren't right.

“Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” From here on out, you are not going to say, well, my daddy was wicked, so I am just going to be wicked by default. No, you are going to change it.

Verse 14 shows the son who does: “Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like”. The son sees everything his father did, considers it, and does not do the same. A son can see it and change.

So the proverb is broken by a son who looks at his father's ways with open eyes. The iniquity we were shapen in is real, but it is not a sentence we have to serve; the son who considers and does not do such like is the proof that it can be changed.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 18:19-20
precepts.why:
The people still asked, “Yet say ye, Why? doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father?” That is the sour grapes proverb again. The Lord answers: “When the son hath done that which is lawful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father”.

In other words, yes, intergenerational trauma is real. But do you just sit in it, or do you change? This son changed. If there is a son who changes and does what is right according to the Lord, he is not going to die, although his father will. Just because our fathers were wicked, just because our mothers didn't know God's laws and taught us evil, that is not an excuse to stay in this. That trauma is real; you must recognise it and move on from it.

“neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.” Each soul answers for itself.

And the Lord still has mercy on the sick. Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick”, and “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” That is every last one of us. Although we have been through trauma and traumatic experiences, we cannot use the excuse of what we have been through anymore. Christ has given us a clean slate, and the way to walk in it is to keep his statutes and do them.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the understanding and wisdom was given to us, not to the other nations. So there is no reason for you to sit on that wisdom and do nothing.

So we are not supposed to just sit here and do absolutely nothing. Our God saw fit to walk with us, teach us and guide us, and we have to do the same thing: teach our brothers and sisters and wake them up. precepts.label: Acts 1:6
precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come.” Christ said to pray for the Lord's kingdom to come on earth. We are joint heirs with him, so what are we actually praying for? Our kingdom as well.

“When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The apostles, when they came together, asked Christ to restore the kingdom to Israel. So Christ's kingdom is Israel's kingdom as well. We are asking Christ to bring us the kingdom, because we are joint heirs with him.

We have always wanted to know when it is coming. Ezra asked it: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall be the end of the first world we are subjugated to, in bondage under, and the beginning of our kingdom, where the saints can rejoice in glory? The disciples asked it on the mount of Olives: “Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” Christ told them to learn the parable of the fig tree: when the branch is tender and puts forth leaves, you know summer is nigh. “So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” When you see the decadence of this society, know that the tribulation and the destruction are near, even at the doors.

And God told Ezra what to watch: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Jacob's hand held fast Esau's heel for a reason. When Esau goes down, we come up; when Esau is destroyed, we are in our kingdom. That's why the churches don't teach about Esau: the people at the top know, and they make sure it's hidden. So every time you pray thy kingdom come, you are praying for the destruction of the present kingdom. Christ's kingdom is not going to rule beside Babylon the Great; Christ isn't setting a throne beside the president.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
“Thy will be done in earth.” The Lord's will will be done in earth, because this is the will that we want. David said it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The laws of God are within our hearts, so we want what God wants. That's why he says be ye perfect, even as our Father is perfect. The objective is to become one with him: one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That's the hierarchy the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs, his ambassadors on this earth, and that's why he gave us the name Israel. We are the prince of his power. That's us, not anybody else.

If the will of God is going to be done in this earth, and there is a will here already, then this will has got to be destroyed. Two kings cannot sit on the same throne. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” Notice: is given. Esau took the planet and ruled it in evil, yes, but God gave him the power to do so, for a time, and when that time is up it's over.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” Esau struts with his chest out, bombing countries and stealing their resources, their minds, their women, and everybody wants to look like him. And the Most High says, I'm the one who put him up there, so that I can destroy him and everybody will know I'm the true power. The Lord endures with longsuffering because he will not break his word: he gave this man a time to rule, until the times of the nations be fulfilled. The whole nation of Edom is the vessels of wrath, a channel through which God shows how angry and how powerful he is, fitted to destruction, created for that purpose, just as he set up Pharaoh.

These are diabolical, demonic people; look at James Byrd dragged through the streets of Jasper, Texas. That's not teaching hatred; it's the facts. There's no such thing as a nice snake. Stick by these commandments. Come out from among them, be separate, gather yourselves together, organize and prepare for your kingdom while he brings this kingdom down. That is the maturing we have to do.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-2
precepts.why:
The believers in Acts 4 “were of one heart and of one soul” and “had all things common”. To keep from losing ourselves, selling ourselves out and losing our souls, we have to grow the same way. Paul shows what pulls us away: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

The seducing spirits are money and wealth, the many things that distract us from God, from Christ and from our purpose in life. We live in an era where vanity is a drug and attention is a drug. At the blitz last week, kids said they want to be streamers. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer, the things that actually build nations? That is why we have been destroyed as a people. And there are men and women in the faith who want to leave this and go to the world and stream.

The “doctrines of devils” are religion, man-made religion. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy” is politics: a lie that makes you feel assimilated into a government that is kicking you out of it. If you are Israel, what they call black, you cannot be in their government. There is one black governor in this whole country, and all the black generals have been taken out as not qualified. They are making their country great again in their eyes.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron.” Religion, politics and the gifts of this world sear the conscience. Money, riches and comfort should not be your god; the American dream is a lie. Having all things in common, in faith and understanding, is what keeps us from departing from the faith.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:1-5
precepts.why:
“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.” In perilous times we have to start having all things in common, like the believers of Acts 4, and build our faith.

“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: going for likes, not worried about being an aid to your society or your community. It is me, me, me: how many likes and followers do I have? It is not about you, negro. It is about your people. “Covetous, boasters”: boasting of vanity, money, drugs, houses, cars, women. “Proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: not appreciative of God and what he has done for you. “Unholy, Without natural affection”.

This is the nature of them that go after the world, that go after the gift that destroys the heart. The one who is a lover of himself holds on to what he has; the believers in Acts 4 said none of the things they possessed was their own.

So we have to stop living beyond our means and be content with our wages and content in life. A family of seven may need a house with a little room, but if you are a single brother, why are you buying a mansion and expensive cars? Do you know the times we are living in? There is coming a time when you will not be worrying about maintaining your BMW. Riches and comfort, keeping up with the Joneses and the American lie of a dream, should not be your god.

precepts.label: Acts 4:34-35
precepts.why:
The same chapter shows what having all things common looked like: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

That is the point. We have to begin to live below our means, not beyond them. This nation of ours is a big nation, and there are millions of our people that lack. When you sacrifice your much, it is much to them that have little.

The only way to experience that, to let what you have help those who have little, is to travel. We must go and spread this gospel abroad, and that is part of why we go out into the nations.

The believers of Acts 4 had prayed, the place was shaken, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost and spake the word with boldness. Out of that came one heart and one soul, and out of one heart and one soul came a people among whom no one lacked. That is the same order we need now: faith first, and then a nation that looks after its own.

precepts.label: James 1:21-25
precepts.why:
In Galatians Paul says you are not justified by the works of the law, and Christians say, see, we don’t have to keep the commandments; Christ died for us, just believe. Then the same Paul writes, “For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” Was Paul schizophrenic? No. The law in Galatians is animal sacrifice, explained in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, which Christ did away with. The law here is the commandments. Faith comes first, and then the works follow.

Christ’s brother James answers the same way: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness”: lay aside all sin. “And receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The engrafted word is the law and the testimony. Some heard in church that the law cannot save you, only Christ can. The law in Christ saves you; keeping God’s commandments can save your soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” That takes you right back to Romans 2:13. Christianity tells you that you do not have to keep God’s commandments and will still be saved; they deceive themselves and others. “For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” He reads the Bible, says yeah okay, and goes back to sinning, looking in the mirror and forgetting what he saw.

“But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.” The work is the commandments; blessed in his deed is justified. Christ gave us liberty from the law of sin and death, the sacrifices under which a man “died without mercy”, but that liberty is not freedom from doing the commandments. The doers of the law shall be justified.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
James says, “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” What is the engrafted word? Isaiah answers it: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

The law and the testimony is the word. So the word James says is able to save your soul, the word we must be doers of and not hearers only, is the law and the testimony: the commandments of God.

That is why Paul could say, “not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” The law he means there is the commandments, the engrafted word, not the sacrifices that Christ did away with.

So when the church says the law cannot save you, they are not speaking according to this word. Those who speak not according to the law and the testimony have no light in them. The word saves, Christ saves, and the doer of the word is the one justified.

Paul proves from the Psalms that Israel became filthy: “They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” The whole nation was broken. Jeremiah laments that same breaking: “What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?”

A breach is a split or a tear. Our breach is great like the sea. Who can heal us? Christ, our saviour.

Isaiah shows the healing: “And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.” When our souls are in drought, the Lord is going to water us and heal us. “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”, the waste places we made when we became filthy. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.”

The root word of reparations is repair. The repairer of the breach: that is the reparations right there. Both Jews and Gentiles, Judah and Ephraim, were “all under sin” and torn apart, and the one who heals that breach is Christ, repairing and restoring Israel.

precepts.label: Acts 15:14-17
precepts.why:
Paul says “we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin”, and the Gentiles there are Israelites. Acts 15 shows the same Gentiles being restored: “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” That references what took place in Acts 10, and we understand that is talking about Israel.

“And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”. Build again: that is the reconciliation, that is the reparation. It had fallen down because we became filthy, and God restores the waste places. Who is that? All twelve tribes of Israel.

Then verse 17: “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”. The residue is the rest of the nations outside of the twelve tribes: Edom and the others. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: that is the Christians, and the Jews.

They try to include themselves in our reconciliation, our restoration and our adoption. But the building again is of David’s tabernacle, the twelve tribes; the residue only seeks after the Lord once Israel is set up again.

precepts.label: Amos 9:11-12
precepts.why:
Acts 15 quotes the prophet Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. The breaches are the tear, the split, like the breach “great like the sea” in Lamentations. Remember, the root word of reparations is to repair.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. This is the restoring of Israel, both kingdoms that Paul proved “are all under sin” in Romans 3, repaired and raised up as in the days of old.

Then: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.” That they, all twelve tribes, may possess the remnant of Edom and of the heathen called by his name.

So you see, other nations cannot be involved in our reconciliation, our restoration or our reparation. The ones called by his name, the Christians and the Jews, are not the tabernacle being raised; they are what Israel possesses once it is raised. This goes back to the classes before on Romans 11 and Acts 10.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 10:33
precepts.why:
Romans 4:2 says “For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.” What works is Paul talking about? Nehemiah condenses them into one verse: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Continual means it was done all the time, daily, annually. And “to make an atonement” goes back to the word justify: atone, justify and reconcile are the same thing. So the works Paul is talking about are temple sacrifice, temple law. When Paul wrote, the temple was still standing and the Jews in Rome were still going to it and still sacrificing, and they believed their works were enough.

Abraham shows the order. In Genesis 15 the Lord promised the old man an heir out of his own bowels and seed as the stars, “And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.” He was promised the land and he believed. Only then was he told to take the heifer, the goat, the ram and the birds and divide them. Faith came first, then the works.

When brothers don't study Paul's letters, they start saying Paul's letters are not authoritative, and speak evil of dignities, of Paul, Mark and Luke, because they weren't of the twelve. When you speak evil of dignities, your mind is blinded and you end up teaching a whole different gospel: that the nations can be saved. House negroes are the worst kind of negro. But this is the college course of this school. Know what the works are from Nehemiah, and nobody can come to your school or camp and confound you at Romans 4.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:28
precepts.why:
Romans 4:4 says “Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.” To him that offers sacrifices, the reward is not reckoned of grace or mercy, but of debt, because under Moses there was no grace. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. Without mercy means without grace.

If you chose to do something worthy of death that an animal could not atone for, you had to die. If you broke the Sabbath, you couldn't atone with an animal. Homosexuality, you couldn't atone with an animal. Idolatry, you couldn't atone with an animal. And if you chose not to sacrifice at all, you had to die. So you were indebted to offer continual sacrifices all the time: continual burnt offerings, drink offerings, sin offerings.

The prophets said the temple would be destroyed. Once the temple is gone, where are your works? If your salvation rests on sacrificing an animal and there is no animal, no priest and no temple to atone with, by default you have condemned yourself. That is why faith in Christ has to supersede the works.

“But to him that worketh not”, him that does not offer sacrifice, “but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.” Christ justifies the ungodly through his death. Just as with Abraham, who was counted faithful before he sacrificed animals, God “imputeth righteousness without works”. Israel could keep sacrificing while the temple stood, but Christ had to come first in their minds, or they were in debt.
