precepts.label: Isaiah 53:4-12
precepts.why:
Paul says Christ “was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.” Our offences: whose? Isaiah 53 shows who Christ was delivered for. “Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows”: this is Isaiah speaking of his people. “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.” Maybe you are thinking that is everybody. Keep reading.

“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.” Like sheep of the house of Israel. The us is the sheep. “He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth”; he did not say one word. Then: “for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.” Not all people, not all nations, not the good nations, not the not-so-bad ones. My people. And Isaiah was an Israelite. Now you know who the our is, who the all is, who the we is.

All the apologists online have to do is show us in the Old Testament where this changed and Christ came back a second time and died for heathens. Show where Isaiah says, oh yeah, I almost forgot the other nations. Peter said the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul’s letters as they do the other scriptures, but this is what Paul got it from.

“By his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.” Many who? Israelites; the thought has not changed. “He bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.” An intercessor is a mediator, someone who steps in and dies in your place. There is no Isaiah 53 part two for the other nations. Abraham believed without the works of sacrifice, and so must we: faith in the one delivered for our offences.

precepts.label: Daniel 9:24-26
precepts.why:
Christ was delivered for our offences. Daniel shows the same thing on the prophetic clock: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. Seventy weeks, 490 years, upon thy people: Daniel’s people, Israel.

For what? “To finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” That is what Christ did when he died. Reconciliation goes back to the word atonement, and back to the word justification.

“From the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem”: the rebuilding under Persia. “Unto the Messiah the Prince”: Rome. “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”. He would be killed, but not for himself. Who was he killed for? His people. That is what Isaiah said, and that is why Daniel says not for himself.

“And the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Titus and Vespasian. “And the end thereof shall be with a flood”: war, 70 AD. “And unto the end of the war desolations are determined”: Israel removed out of the land and scattered among all nations into slavery. When the temple was destroyed there was no priest and no temple left to atone with, so the one who put his faith in the animal instead of Christ condemned himself by default. Faith in Christ had to come first.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:25
precepts.why:
Isaiah 53 says “by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many”. Somebody says, see, many means anybody. Isaiah has something for that: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Not all the seed of Israel and anybody else outside of Israel. Not all the good nations. Not individual heathens who say they have black friends. All the seed of Israel, all twelve tribes, shall be justified.

How? My righteous servant justifies many by dying on the cross, by laying on himself the iniquity of them all. That is the “justification” Paul speaks of when he says Christ “was raised again for our justification”, and it is why Romans 5 opens, “Therefore being justified by faith”. Who, according to the Old Testament, would be justified? Israel.

So when you read justification all throughout Paul’s letters, there should be no confusion about what he is talking about or who he is talking about. Abraham’s faith was imputed to him for righteousness, and “it was not written for his sake alone”, but for his seed who believe on him that raised up Jesus from the dead.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:13-16
precepts.why:
“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Christ came and died for his people; he was cut off for his people. Romans 5:9 says we are “justified by his blood”, and Ephesians says it is that same blood that brings near those who were far off.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one”. That is the peace of Romans 5:1, “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ”. And it shows who is being spoken of. Who is the both? The two nations. When you read the history in the book of Kings, Israel and Judah split apart into two kingdoms, and Ezekiel prophesied that our king would come and die for the nation of Israel and the nation of Judah, so that they would no longer be two nations but one nation under Christ.

He “hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace”. What was two is now one new man, with no more division.

“And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”. That is the same word as Romans 5:10, “we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”. Reconcile means to bring together again, and the both being reconciled are the southern and northern kingdoms. So the audience in Romans is the same people God spoke to in the old covenant: the Jews in the church at Rome, and with them the Gentiles, who are the northern kingdom. Christ, by his death, brought both houses back to the Father as one.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 6:49
precepts.why:
Romans 5:11 says “by whom we have now received the atonement”, and the margin gives the word reconciliation. Atonement is Christ’s death, which brings us back to the Father. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word; that is also called adoption. Atonement is reparation for a wrong or injury: when Christ died on the cross he died for our wrongs. Break the word down in English and it is at-onement: bringing back together again as one. Who did God come to bring together as one? Israel, the two sticks joined together, both kingdoms.

So who was the atonement ever made for? “But Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, and were appointed for all the work of the place most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.” For Israel. Not for everybody.

The theology of the world says atonement is the reconciliation of God and all humankind. But God was never one with all humankind. All nations were never one with Israel, ever. The priesthood of Aaron made atonement for one people, and when Christ made the atonement with his own body, he made it for that same people.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 29:23-24
precepts.why:
In the days of Hezekiah, “they brought forth the he goats for the sin offering before the king and the congregation; and they laid their hands upon them: And the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel: for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.”

All means all twelve, because Hezekiah was trying to bring them back together: all twelve tribes, and the strangers that showed up for the Passover.

Here reconciliation and atonement stand side by side, and they were made through the blood of animals. When Christ died, his body replaced them. That is why Romans 5:9 says “being now justified by his blood”: his blood replaces the animals, the works we no longer receive justification from. And the time came, as Daniel 9 foretold, when the temple was destroyed, the priests scattered abroad and not one stone left standing. With no way left to atone with animals, we had to have faith in Christ; otherwise you condemn yourself, indebted to a law you can no longer keep.

So atonement, reconciliation and justification are three words for the same thing, for the same people, with the same God. Reconciliation is the restoration of a friendly relationship, a reuniting; you cannot reunite with someone you were never joined to. Israel was with God before, rebelled until “he was turned to be their enemy”, and through the death of his Son was brought back again. That is Romans 5:10: “when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 3:5-27
precepts.why:
“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men”. Yes, it passed upon all men; all nations are capable of sinning. The question is who God held accountable. Ezra tells the story. God “gavest a body unto Adam”, breathed into him the breath of life, and “unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The evil in Adam passed into all nations; Cain and them were wicked by default.

But out of Adam came a specific line God wanted to keep his laws. The flood came, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men”: not Ham’s or Japheth’s line, but Shem’s, the righteous line of Seth. They multiplied and “began again to be more ungodly than the first”, so God chose Abraham: “Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”. Judith shows Abraham’s people left the gods of their fathers in Chaldea and worshipped the God of heaven. God promised “that thou wouldest never forsake his seed”, and “As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau”. There is always that special line God deals with.

At Sinai he gave “the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel. And yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart”. “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The same evil that was in Adam passed on to the righteous line. Then David built the city, and “they that inhabited the city forsook thee, And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done: for they also had a wicked heart: And so thou gavest thy city over into the hands of thine enemies.”

It is a repeated cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets God’s laws, goes against them, destruction comes, they repent, and out of that line the righteous rise again. The accountability for sin fell on that line. That is what Paul does in Romans 5: he gives the origin story of sin, how it killed off the chosen people, and why Christ had to come and die for that same chosen line.

precepts.label: Romans 8:29-30
precepts.why:
“So by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” Who are the many? Romans 8 answers: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.” Foreknow means knew before. Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.

“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. The called are the elect Peter wrote to, the strangers scattered throughout Galatia and the rest, “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”, “a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation”.

“And whom he called, them he also justified”: justified through the blood of Christ. “And whom he justified, them he also glorified”: as Isaiah says, “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Amos says it plainly: “You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” All nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel’s sins and sent Christ for them. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” The free gift unto justification of life came upon the people God foreknew.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:1-5
precepts.why:
Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, the same saints as at Rome. Who are the saints? “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” No other nation made a covenant with God by sacrifice.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. As Eve was in Adam, we the bride were in Christ, chosen before the world was founded, “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. The adoption is the reconciliation, the atonement, the justification and the restoration.

So the many made righteous by the obedience of one in Romans 5 are the saints God chose in Christ before the foundation of the world. Adam’s offence brought death on the chosen line, and Christ’s obedience brings them back into the adoption that was always theirs.

precepts.label: Romans 11:1-2
precepts.why:
If sin reigned unto death over the chosen line, has God given up on them? Paul answers: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Which he foreknew: that is Amos 3 and Romans 8 again. “You only have I known of all the families of the earth”, and “whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate”.

The cycle Ezra described, the righteous line receiving the law, going off, being destroyed and repenting, never ended with God throwing his people away. Every time, out of that line the righteous rose up again.

So where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, and it abounded upon the same people God foreknew. Paul, an Israelite of Benjamin, is himself the proof that God has not cast away his people.

precepts.label: Romans 9:3-5
precepts.why:
Paul’s heart is for his own: “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”. His kinsmen according to the flesh: his race. “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

Pertaineth means belongs. The adoption belongs to them, the adoption of Ephesians 1:5. The glory belongs to them: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all belong to the Israelites.

“Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.”

Christ came for Israel. The free gift that came “upon all men unto justification of life” in Romans 5 is the adoption, the glory and the promises that pertain to the Israelites, the people whose sins God held to account from Adam on and whom he justified by the obedience of one.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:28
precepts.why:
“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus”. The condemnation goes back to the curse on him that continueth not in all things written in the law. Almost all things were purged with blood, not all. There were sins no animal could help you atone for, and if you fell under that, you got condemnation: death. You got stoned to death, set on fire, or hung from a tree.

That is “the law of sin and death”, the law of sacrifice. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. He that hated Moses’ law, the law we all agreed to keep, died without mercy. There was no grace under Moses. If you sinned a certain sin against the Lord, you got immediate death. There was no, I’m sorry, I repent, I didn’t mean to. It was death. Condemnation and death are synonymous.

The Most High had mercy on David, on Moses, on Solomon. But you are not David, you are not Solomon, you are not Moses, you are not Esther. Do not even try that, because you will.

“For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh”: the law of sin and death was weak because the people offering the sacrifices were weak and sinful. “The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death”: made me free, given me liberty. By Christ “all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Under the animals you could not repent of everything; under Christ’s death you can. That is why there is now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.

precepts.label: Romans 12:21
precepts.why:
The first step is study, pray and apply: do your research, and then turn from sin. Then we have to learn how to turn all of this evil and mischief into righteousness, from the power of Satan to God, from darkness unto light. Romans 12 lays out the steps: “Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.” Come home, family.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another”: looking out for each other and honoring one another within our marriages, our relationships and our nation. “Not slothful in business”: our business is that we are called by God to magnify the law and increase our faith. “Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord”: doing the work and helping your people. “Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints”. What better life to live than to help your people?

And the chapter ends with the sum of it: “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.” Do not let this world destroy your faith.

How do we overcome? With the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, and knowing who you are. You overcome that evil with the good of this Bible. Love without dissimulation, brotherly love, fervency, patience and prayer are the good that overcomes the evil around us.

precepts.label: Romans 8:13-14
precepts.why:
It is not a sin to drink. But when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation; it is not to be used in that manner. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome these things.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”. To live after the flesh is to obey the elements of the flesh: going to the bottle and making that the outlet. The end of that road is always death, just as Habakkuk 2:12 shows that there is always an evil road, and at the end of it you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. That is where we are. The drinking problem in this land is a quarter trillion dollars, but the commandments fix all of that.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be. So we should not be overcome with that evil; we have to overcome that evil with good, and the good is God's laws.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 31:28-29
precepts.why:
“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind”. Measurably. The wine is not the sin; the measure is the key. “But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. That is the key point: bitterness of the mind.

The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element on the earth was created by the Lord, and it has its function and its purpose. But if you use it and abuse it, you cannot be useful for the nation.

precepts.label: Psalms 111:10
precepts.why:
“Every man’s work shall be made manifest”. What made Israel United in Christ different from the other organizations, some of which started building before us with far more members and resources, yet show no growth, no expansion, no change? The foundation. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”.

That was learned very early in this truth: if they weren't keeping the commandments, they couldn't teach me nothing. You would see different camps outside teaching on the Lord's Sabbath with a beanie on, scarves and head wraps, coffee steaming off the cup, telling you the white man is the damn devil and you need to join a school.

Meanwhile, how do you get to the kingdom? How do I make my marriage better, deal with my wife, deal with my kids? How can I be a better brother? What's the plan, what's the vision? None of that was being taught.

Back in 2006, when everybody was doing YouTube videos, the Bishop's videos weren't getting the hits, because they weren't the conspiracy stuff. But the good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments, and that is the foundation this body was built on.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:18
precepts.why:
“Where there is no vision, the people perish”. Early on there was really no direction in the other camps. In 2006 one of the biggest things taught was that 9/11 was an inside job. Israelites were doing hour-long videos on the back of the dollar bill: connect the words, it says Mason on it. There was FEMA camp doctrine, that we were all going to get killed and put in plastic coffins at Walmart. People were scared to go to Walmart. Their focus wasn't on the right thing.

Some brothers said, we're going to take to the streets and talk crazy to white folks and at the women as they walk by. Where has that gotten them today? Who grew a congregation by hating the black woman, the white man and all the other nations? Whose congregation is thriving with that as the basis of its teaching?

The Nathaniel 7 page separated many so-called teachers from those who actually feared God and understood the mission. Having a vision, a plan for our people and for the kingdom, is part of the foundation laid on Christ. Without it, the work burns and the people perish.

precepts.label: Romans 12:2
precepts.why:
Rather than roll with those that had no vision, the choice was to stand with those that decided to turn against the ways of the world: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

It was clear this was the right place when surrounded by men and women who decided to put everything else behind them and not be conformed to this present world, who decided, we are going to do what God said.

It may not be fashionable. At one point fringes weren't fashionable; now everybody's mama wants fringes. At one point it wasn't fashionable for women to be in a dress, fully covered in modest apparel. They said, y'all are oppressing them women. No, we are not oppressing them; we are giving them what God said.

That is building on the right foundation. Those who do his commandments have a good understanding, and that is why you are here as well.

precepts.label: Matthew 7:24-25
precepts.why:
“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Christ tells us how to build on him: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock”.

These sayings of mine are Christ's words. What did Christ say? If you love me, keep my commandments. What else did he say? That anybody teaching against keeping the commandments is going to be least in the kingdom of heaven.

This is what we have done here. We have built this house, this congregation, this organization on Christ, on the laws of God and faith in him. We surrounded ourselves with those who decided to build on the proper foundation, and that is why this house stands.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:12
precepts.why:
Look at the back of your shirts, brothers. We have built this congregation, this body, on the faith in Christ and the commandments of God: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Is there any other way to build? Can you be successful any other way? No.

That is the foundation Paul says no man can lay other than Christ. For those in the Israelite camps who want to know the secret, the secret is keeping the laws, from the beginning. As long as we stand in the spirit, the Most High God is going to bless us and you'll see the growth. When another camp asked how we set up schools in different states and countries all over the world, the answer was: we keep the commandments and faith in Christ. The Lord is not going to bring the believers to you if you haven't been sent.

precepts.label: Psalms 127:1
precepts.why:
Build any other way and it is going to fall. “Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.”

Go ahead and try to do it another way. A lot of these organizations are finding out what happens when you build on anything other than the Lord. Some built their whole congregation on fear. They ran to Egypt because they thought the judgment was coming in 2012. Brothers got their passports, not to go teach but to try to deliver themselves; they left Babylon and literally led their people into a civil war, talking about safety and security. We are not built like that; this foundation is built on the rock.

Black people have the attitude that we can't build anything for ourselves and that the other nations, especially the white man, have to get involved for us to succeed. We have a totally different mindset. The Bishop always taught: make sure we have our own and never depend on anybody, because the enemy can shut you down any minute. Nobody is backing us up, and we don't need anybody to. We need each other. Together we can move mountains.

That is why we have had the success we've had: the Lord built the house. And this is just the beginning; you have not seen anything yet.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:23
precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Paul is not making anything up. He is not creating a list and saying, I'll place this person here and that person there. He went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning, when Adam named his wife Eve, and he does it in other places too.

Ephesians says it again: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Is there any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church.

So the order runs: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or out of their position, what are they? The damn devil. That goes for the men too: men who step out of their role and want to be a mama's boy, you are the damn devil. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

There cannot be a commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle with something, and we know the fight, but never be the one who says, I can get with everything else but that right there I just can't do; he's an idiot, I can't follow him. That is not what the scripture said.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:18
precepts.why:
“the head of every man is Christ”. Colossians shows it: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead”. Christ is the head of the church.

And Christ himself is under a head: “the head of Christ is God.” Christ said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do”. And, “the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth”. How could the Father show the Son if the Son was the Father? If you are still stuck on the Trinity, go sit in the corner. It makes no sense for the Most High to show his Son something if they are the same entity.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given, and the headship of the household falls under the same order. “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” To honour the Son is to honour what he said; if you do not honour the order God has given you, you are not honouring the Lord.

Christ said, “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He is letting us know that he himself is in the divine order and submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did?

We are one body, in the same mind and the same spirit, so wherever you travel it should have the same feel and the same teachings.

Ephesians says it: “There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

There are not multiple ways, no matter what Oprah said. There are not different types or different forms of God and how to worship God. That is what brought us together. If fellowship, friendships and relationships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. We are brothers and sisters who decided to do what God said against all odds and all the influences of the world; we don't care if you look at us funny.

We keep coming back to that soundness, that unity, that oneness in Christ. Anybody teaching anything other than that does not belong here. There is no separatism in the nation and no separatism in the body of Christ. We are all one.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:11-13
precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord is not the author of confusion; he is of order. When he brings in these different talents, gifts and members, he brings them for a purpose that serves one thing, with different functions. Paul shows it: “And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”.

All of it was for one goal: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for the perfecting of the saints.

You see it in the teachers today. Not all of them focus on the same things: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage, and you can see, that's his specialty. Learning from the deacons as the first internet member, you could see, he's good at this, I need some of that, and you learn where to go and what to glean.

What office can we say we don't need? If you think like that, you're not nation building; you haven't been given the vision. Back in the day some camps said, don't do anything with the videos, just play them. But the video needs music, an intro, something alluring, so someone outside the scriptures says, let me look at this, and once the scriptures start hitting: oh snap, I know who I am now. That effort is a member doing its part.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 4:10
precepts.why:
Every member was set in the body for a reason, so Peter says: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.”

Shame on you if you come in here and sit on your hands, sit on the talent God has given you, and put forth no effort. If you have a craft or something to offer and you don't come in trying to show it and help, shame on you. You have been given that for a reason.

Your job is to utilize that gift and benefit your nation. Nobody should be bogging down your talents or making you stagnant; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching them to others where possible. That is being a good steward: the gift is ministered one to another, so the whole body is built up.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:16
precepts.why:
“A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.” When you have a talent, when you're able to do something for the nation, at least come in and say, hey, I'm able to do this. We may say, all right brother, we'll utilize that gift a little later, or, we need you right here right now.

When the building in OKC was first acquired around 2017, it was trash. Out of nowhere brothers started coming out of the woodwork: I heard y'all teaching, I want to join. One saw them working on the building and said, I'm a carpenter, I build. It was dangerous in there, with downed wires, mold, asbestos and fiberglass floating; some brothers probably have lung damage to this day. He looked around and said, that's a fire hazard, you're going to die if you mess with that wire.

They were in there on the strength of the Lord, tearing down to build. The Lord brought those people in so they could build up the school. And right after completion that same brother disappeared: he served his purpose.

So a gift is not for hiding. It makes room for the man and brings him where the Lord wants him, and the body is built because every member brings what God gave him.

precepts.label: Matthew 25:24-28
precepts.why:
We have to utilize the gifts God gives us in this truth. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security. Realize that when you don't use it, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take the truth even further. The parable of the talents shows it; the talent is money, standing for the understanding God bestows on you.

“Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth”. He hid that understanding, that gift, and did nothing with it.

Watch what Christ says: “Thou wicked and slothful servant”. “Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.” Even if you couldn't do anything else, you could have put it with the exchangers so something could be reaped. “Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.”

We have seen it time and again: brothers and sisters with talents who hide them, or hold them over us: you can't do this without me. Know that yes, it can be done without you. If you can't be used, you are useless. But none of you are useless. We all have been called for a reason; there is something in you that you have to give to build the nation. The quicker we understand that, the quicker we get out of here.

precepts.label: Romans 12:3
precepts.why:
God has given us different gifts and different offices but the same mission. So Paul says, “to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” We are all expendable; we can all be replaced if we don't put something into this truth.

What happens when someone thinks more highly than he ought? Just because you're the knuckle, the one who keeps us safe, you think you're better than everybody else. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices as less important.

Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters who clean the toilets, the kitchen and the floors? Infested with roaches and mice. Without the kitchen? Hungry as hell; some single brothers look forward to the Sabbath because they get a real meal and not the peanut butter and jelly they're used to. The Lord brought all these administrations together so we can function. Not one is more important; they all play a part.

Even leadership. A deacon is not better than you; he could die tomorrow and be the devil. He has to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. At the gas company nobody says, oh, that's Deacon; they say, nigga, I had to come shut your stuff off for you to come see me. No one cares. If you start to think you're better because of your office, this body will suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into the earth, and it may have been you who got one.

precepts.label: Philippians 2:3
precepts.why:
One body, many members, so “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.”

That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some of you security brothers, be careful. Because you're able to say move over here, move over there, you get ahead of yourself playing musical chairs: get up, go over here, no, sit right here, don't say nothing, hop on one leg, Simon says shut up. That's your brother; that's your sister. Deal with somebody the way you want to be dealt with.

Yes, some folks are hard-headed and act a straight fool, and sometimes you have to speak a certain way to let them know you're serious, because some don't understand organization. But no member is better than the next. We are all the same, working toward the same goal: we want the kingdom.

If we have this mind frame, esteeming each other better than ourselves, we are going to move mountains. That is what it means that the many members are yet but one body.

precepts.label: Romans 12:4
precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” God organizes the body, and God is who made us great. We are at the forefront, considered the vanguard, because God appointed us to be; if we move any differently than that, God will remove us and put somebody else there. Each of us was gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation.

Romans says the same: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. Why do the members not have the same office? The heart and the brain function in different ways, but they come together to make the body function as one. The mind does not have the same function as the hand, and the hand does not have the same function as the foot. Every member functions, but they all need each other.

The body could not function with all hands or all elbows. If everybody comes in trying to be the hands, or everybody trying to be the feet, what will happen? Disorder. Everybody cannot be the head; everybody cannot be the shoulders. Everybody has their function.

So for those who think you are insignificant, just a regular Joe: God called you in here, and you have a mission and a purpose. You had better apply your gifts and your talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God. And preparing as a nation means more than food and water: we need lawyers, doctors, nurses, farmers. Go to school; master any skill, any trade, and bring that mastery back to benefit your nation.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 14:40
precepts.why:
God set the members in the body “as it hath pleased him”, and Paul says: “Let all things be done decently and in order.” The Lord is about order. He is not going to keep bringing the same member into the body, just hands and more hands; that is not how this works.

Understand how the scriptures use the body: it goes into functions. Can everybody be a teacher? Then who is going to read? Can everybody be the one for camp? Change is coming, because we have grown into a nation, and there are many talents and gifts, especially among the sisters, that have not even been tapped into yet.

We have looked at this from a war perspective, and it is all-out war outside; we need brothers prepared to spread this gospel. But in the functioning of this body, the Lord is showing that there are many more things we have to prepare ourselves for. If we don't, we will stay stagnant like others have. The camps that taught their people not to go to school, because Christ is coming soon, cannot open one building to this day, because they taught their people not to achieve greatness.

God brings the different members in for a purpose that all serves the same thing, with different functions. Back in 2016 the vision was set forth: Original Royalty, the kitchen, the school with the kids, security, video, music, all components of a society, the body of Israel under Christ working together for the common good of the whole nation. What was vision then is old news now; that is what order and vision do for a nation.

“because it will surely come, it will not tarry”. precepts.label: Revelation 18:2-4
precepts.why:
“but rather that ye may prophesy”. The purpose of prophecy is to build your spirit up and prepare you for temptation and destruction. Prophecy is warning: thus saith the Lord. When you see these things come to pass, know that Esau, Edom, America, is the enemy the Bible speaks of.

Revelation 18 gives the warning plainly. Babylon the great is fallen and has become the habitation of devils, and the call goes out: “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

Come out of religion. Come out of these doctrines. Come out of Christianity. Come out of the lies and philosophies and deceit, and repent. The Christian church has you clapping on a tambourine while the prophecy is fulfilled before your eyes; they say the book of Revelation is sealed and cannot explain any of this.

That is why we covet to prophesy: so our people can see who Babylon is, come out of her, and not receive her plagues when the fire comes on her.

precepts.label: Isaiah 47:1-3
precepts.why:

People try to say Babylon is somewhere else, but when has America been touched? The one thing that ever happened, they blew up themselves: 9/11 was the biggest controlled demolition anybody has ever witnessed. The virgin means she has not been touched, defiled or destroyed, until these prophecies are fulfilled. She is going to be touched.

“for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”. She thought she was tender and delicate, but that is coming to an end. As Daniel 2 showed, all manner of nations are within her, including her enemies: sleeper cells.

“Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers.” A virgin would be covered, but here her locks, leg and thigh are uncovered: the wickedness of Babylon, America, is being revealed.

“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” What shame? precepts.label: Acts 13:38-39
precepts.why:
Paul says we are “able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.” The letter is the old testament, the Mosaic law of sacrifice. The spirit is Christ's death. The letter kills: if you despised Moses' law, you died without mercy. We read earlier that almost all things are purged with blood. Almost all things you could atone for, if there was an animal for it. But if there was no animal for it, whose blood got shed? Yours. That is condemnation, and condemnation and death are the same.

How does the spirit give life? “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins”. That is life. “And by him all that believe are justified from all things”. Not almost all things: all things. Everything you can think of, Christ died for, which the animals could not do. You can repent under Christ's death; under animals, you cannot.

“from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses”: that law is the sacrifice, the law of sin and death, the ministration of condemnation. That is why Paul said in Galatians that if you want to go by that sacrifice, you are a debtor to do the whole law, including sacrificing animals, and the temple is destroyed, so you had better figure it out.

So the ministration of death, “written and engraven in stones”, was glorious, but “much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory”, because under Christ you can atone for everything you could not atone for under Moses. “where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty”: freedom from the law of sin and death.

precepts.label: James 1:14
precepts.why:
Paul fears “lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted”. Satan is able to see what is within you, and that is what he attacks: not the stuff you are strong in, but the stuff you are weak in. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” The temptation comes from something already within you.

So if you have a problem with wanting to be the head honcho, wanting to be over your husband, wanting to be the shot caller in control of how things go in the home, Satan plays with that, and you will look up and there will be a complete role reversal in your home. Subtle means pleasing to the senses in a mild or nuanced way. That little bit of power feels good: I decide what we eat around here, I put up the curtains, I picked this out. Then you start overstepping your bounds and do not even know it was Satan who set you up with the curtains. Sisters, when you start to overstep your divine place and purpose, say, that's Satan, you almost got me.

Most of us have been infected by the westernized mindset: birthdays, baby showers, Mother's Day and Father's Day, Thanksgiving, the ring on the finger, rules God did not make that we think are how life is supposed to be. The same goes for how a man deals with his wife. A father who told his son, get your money, the hoes are going to come, and left a condom on his dresser for him, normalized it. That residue has to be let go completely, or it will cloud your judgment and ruin your marriage.

It is the house of the man. Joshua said, as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say, in agreement with my wife. He commanded his home. And some brothers take themselves out of that role and want to be a mama's boy in the marriage, wanting her to mother them instead of leading her. That emboldens her, and now you are her child and that is how she speaks to you. Both are drawn away by their own lust, and Satan works subtly on what is already within.

precepts.label: John 7:35
precepts.why:
Paul keeps saying “among”: the gospel “which I preach among the Gentiles”, preaching him “among the heathen”. Why does he keep using that word? Because Israel was scattered among the nations, and that is who he is writing to the entire time. Then he says “the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter”. Christ wrought effectually in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, “the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles”.

Who are those Gentiles? John answers: “Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The Jews here are the circumcision, born and raised in the Mosaic law. They ask where Christ will go that they cannot find him. Will he go to the dispersed? The dispersed are the Israelites, the diaspora scattered among the Gentiles.

And what do the Jews call those dispersed Israelites? Gentiles: “and teach the Gentiles”. So now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to throughout the entire time. It should be a no-brainer now.

That is why James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision”: Paul to the Israelites scattered among the nations, the others to the Jews who were not scattered abroad. And it is why Paul withstood Peter at Antioch. Peter ate with these Gentiles, the scattered Israelites he was teaching who they are, then withdrew when certain came from James, fearing them of the circumcision. You cannot teach the scattered who they are and then act as if you are not with them; that is a bad example.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 27:15-26
precepts.why:
Galatians 3:10 says, “For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.” Deuteronomy 27 is where Paul is quoting from.

“Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” That is death, and we agreed to it: break these commandments and we would be destroyed. Then it goes down the list. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”, that is, dishonours them. Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark, that maketh the blind to wander, that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow, that lieth with his father's wife. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast”: no animal atones for that. Cursed be he that lieth with his sister or his mother in law, that smiteth his neighbour secretly, that “taketh reward to slay an innocent person.” And every time, all the people said Amen. They agreed to being cursed if they violated these laws.

Then the last: “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.” That is the line Paul quotes. All these things go into morality, civil and moral law, dealing with your brother, your father, your sister; it goes right back to loving thy neighbour as thyself.

That is the curse. Idolatry, adultery, murder, bestiality: there was no repentance and no animal in the temple that could atone for them. The Galatians, the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites, were heavily rooted in idolatry, so under the old covenant they were immediately condemned. That is why Paul asks whether they received the Spirit by the works of the law. If you are under that law of sacrifice, you are under the curse, because what you are guilty of cannot be atoned for under Mosaic law. They came into the faith hearing that Christ had died for them and redeemed them from sins the animals could never cover.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:4
precepts.why:
Galatians 3:11 says, “But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.” The law that cannot justify is the law of sacrifice. Paul is quoting Habakkuk 2:4.

“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. That is Esau. His soul is not right by spirit, by nature, by biology; that nation is not right at all in the spirit or in their heads. “but the just shall live by his faith.” That is where Paul got it.

Abraham's faith was counted for righteousness, and his faith came first, before his works; then his works proved his faith, because they go hand in hand. So the just shall live by faith, and that faith is faith in Christ. The just are those keeping God's laws, the law that is holy, just and good, and they live by faith in Christ, not by the blood of animals.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
What makes you just, so that you live by faith? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.

So when you are just, what are you keeping? God's laws. And what will you live by? Faith in Christ. That is what Habakkuk is talking about when he says the just shall live by his faith, and that is what Paul is talking about in Galatians 3:11. The just are those who keep God's commandments, and they shall live by faith.

So Paul is not throwing away the commandments. The law that cannot justify is the law of sacrifice; the commandments are what make a man just, and the just man lives by faith in Christ.

precepts.label: John 11:49-50
precepts.why:
Caiaphas points out what the curse of the law is. “And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.”

Why would the whole nation perish? Because they were under the old covenant that they agreed to and kept violating over and over again. The northern kingdom went off first, and the southern kingdom fell right after, and both were destroyed by the nations. Standing in the old covenant, based on our own actions and on the law and the prophets, both kingdoms were condemned. By default both were under the curse of the law, which is condemnation. They should have been destroyed.

But the Lord had other plans. He said, I will not destroy them; I love them; I am going to have my son go and die for them, and redeem them from the curse they agreed to in Deuteronomy 27, where all the people said Amen. That is Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us”. The curse and death are the same thing; being made a curse for us means he was killed for us. Christ died to take us out of that contract and put us into a new one, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ”, the northern kingdom.

precepts.label: Acts 3:24-26
precepts.why:
“And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.” The heathen are the Gentiles: the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, justified through faith. But Christians say, see, brother, all nations will be blessed. So what does it mean?

Peter answers: “Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days.” They foretold, as Paul says the scripture foresaw. “Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers”. The ye are the Israelites. Abraham was a prophet, and the covenant passed from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob, “saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.”

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” Unto you first, the Israelites. The blessing is Christ dying for the Israelites, for all of us scattered among all the nations. The earth is too big for us to reach all our people, but Christ's blood covers us wherever we are found. That is how all the kindreds of the earth are blessed: Israel scattered among those nations and blessed with the death of Christ.

And Esau? He already got his blessing: blood and death, slavery, weaponry, war, bloodshed, nukes and witchcraft. He is literally dropping those blessings on Iran right now. He does not need any more. The other nations' blessing is to work, to build up our kingdom, and to survive the destruction as servants. “So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:25
precepts.why:
“foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith”. How do we know who is justified? You will not find anywhere in the law and the prophets that Christ was going to justify, atone for or reconcile all the heathen Gentile nations through his death. What you find is this: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

All the seed of Israel, all the families scattered abroad over the earth, justified by faith in Christ. Whether they are called Jews or called Gentiles, they shall be justified, because Christ died for them among the nations.

Now show me a precept where all the seed of Edom will be justified. All the seed of Moab justified. All the seed of Ishmael, all the seed of the Canaanites. Show me one place. It is nowhere in there.

So “they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham”: the Israelites who have faith in Christ are the children of Abraham, known for his strong faith. Abraham believed God first, and only afterward offered sacrifices, and his faith, not the animal, was counted for righteousness. That is how the seed of Israel is justified, and why “they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 27:15-26
precepts.why:
“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse.” The works of the law, in Galatians 3:2, 3:5, 3:10 and 2:16, is sacrifice, as in Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant. And “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them” is Paul quoting Deuteronomy 27.

What does that curse mean? “Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image”, “And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” Can he atone for it, reconcile with God, find justification? What animal can he use? None. Under the old covenant you get death. That is what cursed means.

So it goes all the way down. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”: disrespects, curses or strikes them. “Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark.” The so-called white man has removed the neighbor's landmark: America is a stolen landmark, Africa is a stolen landmark, Australia is a stolen landmark. How can he atone when the land is still in his possession? He can't; he sits on stolen land. “Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife”, his stepmother. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast.” “Cursed be he that lieth with his sister”, “with his mother in law.” “Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly”: kills his brother secretly and does not get caught. “Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person”: a hitman, a mercenary.

After each one, “all the people shall say, Amen”: we all agreed to it. Then “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them”, which is exactly what Paul quotes. None of these could be atoned for with an animal. It is death all throughout.

That is why those of the works of the law are under the curse. We confirmed to do everything under that covenant of sacrifices, and if you violate a law that no animal can cover, you get the curse, which is death.

precepts.label: Acts 13:38-39
precepts.why:
“But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.” Justified by the law here is the same law as the works of the law in verses 2, 5 and 10 and in Galatians 2:16: the law of sacrifice.

Paul preached the same thing in Acts 13: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Through Christ is preached the forgiveness of sins, and all that believe in Christ's death are justified from all things, all sins.

Could you receive justification from all things under Moses? No, because animals do not atone for all things. Does Christ's death atone for all things, reconcile us from all things, justify us from all things? Yes. That is the difference.

And the law is not of faith because faith came first. “The man that doeth them shall live in them”: the man who does the sacrifices lives until he commits a sin worthy of death, and then he cannot live anymore. The just live by faith in the one whose death covers what no animal could.

precepts.label: John 11:49-52
precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law.” Some people read right past that. What is the curse of the law? Death. But you need a scripture to back up what you say, and John 11 is it.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation, all twelve tribes, perishing: that is the curse of the law. All twelve tribes broke the first covenant, and by that default we were all worthy of death. When Christ died, he took that curse upon himself for us. That is “being made a curse for us”: dying for us.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only.” Not for Judah only, “but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Gather together in one is reconciliation, at-one-ment, atonement.

So Christ died for Judah and for Israel, all twelve tribes. Those scattered abroad are the ones Paul was going to among the heathen, among the Gentiles, while being called Gentiles themselves. That is how “the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 21:22-23
precepts.why:
“for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. That is written in Deuteronomy 21: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled.” Hanging was capital punishment among us.

So Christ took on the curses for us, the punishment and consequence of violating that covenant, when he was hung. Some say he wasn't hung, he was nailed to a cross. But if you are nailed to a wooden pole, you are hanging by your hands and feet. That is a lynching. He was hung for hours.

Peter calls it the same thing, twice: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” And again, “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.” They hung Christ on a tree, on wood, a cross. Christ died a black man's death.

Do you think the lynchings among our people were a coincidence, when the white man hung us from trees and lamps and bridges? People have been hung from time to time, but not to the capacity we have been hung; it was enforced all around among us. The curse of the tree came on our people, and Christ bore that same curse to redeem us from it, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.”

precepts.label: Romans 8:3
precepts.why:
“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” The we is Israel, kept under the law of sacrifice until Christ came on the scene and died for us, the same as Hebrews 9 saying it was imposed until the time of reformation. “Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”: our mentor, our stepping stone, the placeholder for Christ's body being offered in the end. “that we might be justified by faith”: Christ's death justifies us, not the law of sacrifice.

What was it that could not justify? “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh”. The law referred to here is animal sacrifice. Weak through the flesh means through our flesh, and it involves the animals as well. “God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”.

He did away with our condemnation by his own death. As Caiaphas said, it is expedient that one man should die for the people, that the whole nation perish not. Christ ended the condemnation of all twelve tribes by dying on the cross.

So “after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.” Christ has come and gone, and we are all the children of God by faith in Christ, not by animal sacrifice. That was the bewitching earlier in the chapter: that you could be justified without Christ, and all you needed was an animal.

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:18-19
precepts.why:
“For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” What commandment was annulled? Sacrifice. It was annulled for its weakness and unprofitableness, done away in Christ. That is the same weakness as Romans 8:3, the law that was weak through the flesh.

“For the law made nothing perfect”. What law made nothing perfect? Hebrews 10:1 said the sacrifices offered could not make the comers thereunto perfect. It made no man perfect. “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” Not what, but who: Christ is the better hope, and through him we draw nigh unto God.

That is why “after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”. The schoolmaster, the law of sacrifice, was disannulled, and the ye who were kept under it, whether called Jews or Greeks, bond or free, male or female, are the same people of God in Christ.

“And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” The promise pertains to the Israelites. All nations are not the children of promise. If they are, name the nation God calls his people in the old covenant. Isaiah 19 says Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands, but Isaiah 27, Isaiah 11 and Zechariah 10 show that means the children of Israel gathered out of Egypt and Assyria. That is called precepts.

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:9-10
precepts.why:
“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” Who was kept under the law? “Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law”. We were locked into that covenant until Christ came, died, and granted us liberty.

What was it we were kept under? Hebrews gives an example of the works of the law: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrifices could not make him that did them perfect, because sin was already in us since Adam. So the animals had to be temporary.

“Which stood only in meats and drinks”: meat offerings and drink offerings. These are the works of the law read all through Galatians, in 2:16, 3:2, 3:5 and 3:10-11. “and divers washings”: baptisms. “and carnal ordinances”: the traditions of the Pharisees. “imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Forced upon them until the time of reformation, which is the faith that should afterwards be revealed, when Christ came and did away with all of it.

So “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”. The schoolmaster was sacrifice. The sacrificing of animals was a foreshadowing of Christ's death, preparing us for his body. It was temporary, because we grew weary and rebellious behind it and would all have been condemned through it. “But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”: no longer under the law of sacrifice.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 6:1,6
precepts.why:
“There is neither Jew nor Greek”. Christians read it like a soft effeminate man, neither Jew nor Greek, brother, and say it means anybody. The people of Christianity have no idea about history. Why does Paul reference Greeks?

“Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God”. Your law, your culture and your race go hand in hand with God. The Bible says love your neighbour as yourself; that is law. Deny your race and you deny your laws; deny your law and you deny your God.

“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” It was basically illegal under the order of the king to call yourself a Jew or keep Jewish customs. So over time we became Greeks, Gentiles.

That is who Paul is writing to. The ye that were kept under the law in verse 23 are the same ye called Jews and Greeks, bond and free, male and female. Do not escape that context. Whatever your title or status in that present world, Jew or Greek, free like Paul or bond like others, “ye are all one in Christ Jesus”: all God's chosen people.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 4:7-9
precepts.why:
How did Israelites become Greeks? “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest”. Jason was a wicked Israelite who changed his name to Jason, a Greek name. He sought underhandedly to be high priest against his brother Onias, a righteous man, using money to gain authority and leadership. When a man seeks leadership, he usually is not meant to be a leader at all.

“Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents”. He bribed the king of the Greeks, the white man, to force his brother out of position and put him in. “Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise”, a gym, “and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen”: training the Israelite youth in the culture of the Greeks.

“and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.” He registered the Israelites of Jerusalem as citizens of Antioch, the Antioch in Turkey that Paul writes about. Becoming Antiochians was a betrayal of the ancestral laws and a shift to the Greek way of life, and that cultural tension triggered the Maccabean revolt. Antiochian and Greek are the same.

So when Paul says “There is neither Jew nor Greek”, he is writing to the descendants of those same people. Whether called Jew or Greek, “if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” The heirs are Israelites, to whom pertain the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law and the promises.

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:15
precepts.why:
“But when the fulness of the time was come”, the time appointed of the Father, “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.” Who did Christ come to redeem? Them that were under the law. The we is the same we of chapter 3 that were kept under the law, and the adoption pertains to Israel.

Hebrews is the nail in the coffin: “And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” Christ is the mediator of the new testament by means of his death, hanging on the cross. Redemption is the redeeming, and he died for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.

Who was under the first testament? Israel. So those Christ redeemed are those who were under the law, the called who receive the promise of eternal inheritance: the heirs.

“And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.” When Christ died we were no longer servants but sons of the Father, and heirs through his Son.

precepts.label: Romans 8:3
precepts.why:
“But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?” We know the true God now, not a pagan one, and we are known of God because Christ died for us. Verse 3 said we were in bondage under the elements of the world; verse 9 calls them weak and beggarly elements. It is the same bondage the false brethren of chapter 2 wanted to bring us back into. So what are they?

Some say we keep saying law of sacrifice and it does not say that. But it does call it weak. “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”. Weak through the flesh means weak through our sin, through us.

What could the law not do? Hebrews 9:9 says the gifts and sacrifices “could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrificing of animals could not make us perfect. That is what the law could not do, and that is the weak in the weak and beggarly elements.

So God sent his own Son to do what the animals could not, and to turn back to animal sacrifice after knowing God is to desire again to be in bondage.

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:18-19
precepts.why:
Paul calls them “weak and beggarly elements”. Hebrews calls the same thing weak: “For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” The disannulling is of animal sacrifice. What made it weak and unprofitable? “For the law made nothing perfect”, including the man's conscience, “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” That better hope is Christ.

Hebrews 10 says it again: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” It could not make those who offered them perfect.

So the weak and beggarly elements are the sacrificing of animals. They were unprofitable because we were too sinful to keep maintaining them.

That is why verse 10 says “Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years”. Ezekiel 45:17 shows that it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. Colossians 2:16 matches it: meat, drink, holyday, new moon and sabbath days: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and Christ is the body, the sacrifice for all of those things. The Galatians were turning back to observing those days by the weak and beggarly elements.

precepts.label: Acts 15:1-5
precepts.why:
Who was bewitching the Galatians back into bondage? “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” After the manner of Moses, sacrifice followed circumcision, on the eighth day. To be circumcised after the manner of Moses meant going back to sacrifice.

“When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.” These men came from Judea infiltrating and causing confusion, saying you have to sacrifice.

“But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees came in as believers, part of the church, and were imposing that you had to sacrifice according to the manner of Moses. These are the same false brethren brought in unawares that Galatians addresses, who came in privily to spy out our liberty and bring us into bondage.

As the movement grew, the Pharisees went into the churches to win them back to temple law. Paul said he profited in the Jews' religion; people bringing animals was their bread and butter. They were saying to hell with what Christ did, you need an animal for atonement. Paul's answer: if you do, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:22
precepts.why:
“And almost all things are by the law purged with blood”. Almost, not all. So be mindful of always saying blood sacrifice, because the heathen are going to come with that. Not every sin offering was blood, because some among us were poor and could not bring a blood sacrifice.

Leviticus shows it: “But if he be not able to bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon: for it is a sin offering.” The priest took his handful of it as a memorial and burned it on the altar.

And the main example was obedience: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering. He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise. To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” A propitiation is reconciliation. When you depart from sin and keep God's commandments, that is sacrifice enough.

Israel never got there. Israel thought, I can sin all I want and sacrifice all I want, and I'm good. We were children under the schoolmaster, sacrificing and sinning again, going into slavery and out and back again. The Lord said enough of that, and sent his Son. That is why turning back to the weak and beggarly elements is turning back to bondage.
